name: How to apply for a Scotland short-term let licence

step.name: Contact your local council
step.text: Each of Scotland's 32 councils runs its own short-term let licensing process with its own fees. Apply to your local council's licensing team. If you are unsure whether you need a licence or which type fits your property, use the short-term lets checker tool on mygov.scot.

step.name: Prepare your documents
step.text: Councils typically ask for gas and electrical safety certificates, a fire risk assessment, floor plans and proof of building insurance. Check your council's own list before you apply, as requirements vary by council.

step.name: Meet the mandatory conditions
step.text: These include safety standards, maximum occupancy limits and guest information requirements. The mandatory safety conditions include a fire risk assessment, working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, an annual gas safety check by a Gas Safe registered engineer, an electrical safety inspection at least every five years, a Legionella risk assessment, meeting the repairing standard, a valid Energy Performance Certificate issued within the last 10 years, and buildings insurance plus public liability insurance.

step.name: Wait for the council's decision — and do not take bookings yet
step.text: You cannot legally take bookings until your council licence is granted. The council must make a decision within 9 months of receiving a complete application, so apply well before you plan to welcome guests. Operating without a licence is a criminal offence, with a fine of up to £2,500.

step.name: Display your licence number
step.text: Once granted, your licence number should appear on all listings and on your own website. Displaying the number is not the same as holding the licence: planning permission, licensing and safety compliance remain your responsibility.
